## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed service that detects life events such as the birth of a child, job loss, or retirement and would offer eligible families the relevant government support automatically, without an application.

## Problem

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems.

## Delivery Model

The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A small central team would maintain the eligibility rules, and each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability

The initiative plans to be funded from the existing social support budget, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced application processing and fewer appeals. A proposed first phase would cover three life events before expanding.

## What Makes It New

Most government services wait for people to apply. This proposal reverses the direction: the government would come to the citizen at the moment of need, which is rare in social services.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the share of eligible families receiving support, the time from life event to first payment, and citizen satisfaction. A planned comparison with the current application route would test whether uptake improves.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in and a clear record of which data was used. Wrong eligibility decisions would be reduced by keeping a human review step for edge cases.

A proposed service that detects life events such as the birth of a child, job loss, or retirement and would offer eligible families the relevant government support automatically, without an application.

## Problem

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems. The proposal includes a planned small-scale test of a 'decline feedback' channel. This would ask beneficiaries who decline automated offers to optionally share their reasons, to improve targeting and communication. A proposed enhancement to this channel is an optional, structured survey where those declining can select from a short list of pre-defined reasons (e.g., 'I don't trust it,' 'I don't need the support,' 'The offer is unclear') to systematically gather actionable improvement data.

## Delivery Model

The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A proposed enhancement to this model is a hypothetical partnership with a select number of trusted, non-governmental community organizations to act as 'digital navigators' for the phone line and service centers. These navigators would specifically assist non-digital users in understanding and responding to the automated offers, thereby testing an enhanced inclusion model. A small central team would maintain the eligibility rules, and each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability

The initiative plans to be funded from the existing social support budget, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced application processing and fewer appeals. A proposed first phase would cover three life events before expanding.

## What Makes It New

Most government services wait for people to apply. This proposal reverses the direction: the government would come to the citizen at the moment of need, which is rare in social services.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the share of eligible families receiving support, the time from life event to first payment, and citizen satisfaction. A planned comparison with the current application route would test whether uptake improves. Insights from the proposed 'decline feedback' test, including data from the structured survey, would be used to refine these measures. The proposed partnership with community navigators would provide additional data on effectiveness for non-digital users.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in and a clear record of which data was used. Wrong eligibility decisions would be reduced by keeping a human review step for edge cases.

A proposed service that detects life events such as the birth of a child, job loss, or retirement and would offer eligible families the relevant government support automatically, without an application.

## Problem

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems. The proposal includes a planned small-scale test of a 'decline feedback' channel, asking beneficiaries who decline automated offers to optionally share their reasons, to improve targeting and communication. Furthermore, the proposal includes a planned small, targeted test of a 'pre-emptive information' channel. This test would send a brief, plain-language summary of data usage and privacy safeguards alongside the initial offer message, aiming to build trust and increase opt-in rates. A proposed enhancement is a targeted, small pilot to include a 'support package acceptance' option that bundles multiple related benefits (e.g., childcare subsidy + parental leave information) into a single, one-tap acceptance to reduce decision fatigue.

## Delivery Model

The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A proposed enhancement to this model is a hypothetical partnership with a select number of trusted, non-governmental community organizations to act as 'digital navigators' for the phone line and service centers. These navigators would specifically assist non-digital users in understanding and responding to the automated offers, thereby testing an enhanced inclusion model. A small central team would maintain the eligibility rules, and each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability

The initiative plans to be funded from the existing social support budget, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced application processing and fewer appeals. A proposed first phase would cover three life events before expanding.

## What Makes It New

Most government services wait for people to apply. This proposal reverses the direction: the government would come to the citizen at the moment of need, which is rare in social services.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the share of eligible families receiving support, the time from life event to first payment, and citizen satisfaction. A planned comparison with the current application route would test whether uptake improves. Insights from the proposed 'decline feedback' test would be used to refine these measures. The proposed partnership with community navigators would provide additional data on effectiveness for non-digital users. The proposed test of the 'pre-emptive information' channel would provide specific data on its effect on opt-in rates. The proposed pilot for bundled 'support package acceptance' would generate data on its impact on acceptance rates and user feedback on decision fatigue.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in and a clear record of which data was used. The proposed test of the 'pre-emptive information' channel is a planned mitigation aimed directly at building trust around these concerns. Wrong eligibility decisions would be reduced by keeping a human review step for edge cases.

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. This would allow users to proactively and securely flag a life event (e.g., job loss) within the government app to trigger the automated eligibility check, providing a bridge for events not automatically captured by registration systems. In this test, a citizen could authorize a pre-vetted community organization (e.g., a local family center) to receive and help them understand the automated offer on their behalf, specifically for non-digital users.

A proposed service that detects life events such as the birth of a child, job loss, or retirement and would offer eligible families the relevant government support automatically, without an application.

## Problem

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems. The proposal includes a planned small-scale test of a 'decline feedback' channel, asking beneficiaries who decline automated offers to optionally share their reasons, to improve targeting and communication. Furthermore, the proposal includes a planned, small, targeted test of a 'pre-emptive information' channel. This test would send a brief, plain-language summary of data usage and privacy safeguards alongside the initial offer message, aiming to build trust and increase opt-in rates. Additionally, the proposal includes a planned, small-scale test of a 'reverse notification' feature. This would allow users to proactively and securely flag a life event (e.g., job loss) within the government app to trigger the automated eligibility check, providing a bridge for events not automatically captured by registration systems. The proposed test of the 'reverse notification' feature would also include integrating it with a secure, verifiable document upload function for the single most common missing document (e.g., a termination letter), to bridge the gap for events not fully captured in government records. The proposed test would also include a 'life event confirmation receipt' that users can save or share, providing them with a tangible record of their proactive notification to the government. The proposal also includes a planned small-scale test of a 'trusted intermediary' consent model. In this test, a citizen could authorize a pre-vetted community organization (e.g., a local family center) to receive and help them understand the automated offer on their behalf, specifically for non-digital users.

## Delivery Model

The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A proposed enhancement to this model is a hypothetical partnership with a select number of trusted, non-governmental community organizations to act as 'digital navigators' for the phone line and service centers. These navigators would specifically assist non-digital users in understanding and responding to the automated offers, thereby testing an enhanced inclusion model. The proposed test of the 'trusted intermediary' consent model would be integrated into this navigator partnership, allowing authorized organizations to act as formal intermediaries for consenting users. A small central team would maintain the eligibility rules, and each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability

The initiative plans to be funded from the existing social support budget, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced application processing and fewer appeals. A proposed first phase would cover three life events before expanding.

## What Makes It New

Most government services wait for people to apply. This proposal reverses the direction: the government would come to the citizen at the moment of need, which is rare in social services.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the share of eligible families receiving support, the time from life event to first payment, and citizen satisfaction. A planned comparison with the current application route would test whether uptake improves. Insights from the proposed 'decline feedback' test would be used to refine these measures. The proposed partnership with community navigators would provide additional data on effectiveness for non-digital users. The proposed test of the 'pre-emptive information' channel would provide specific data on its effect on opt-in rates. The proposed test of the 'reverse notification' feature, including its integrated document upload function and the 'life event confirmation receipt', would provide data on its usage and effectiveness in capturing life events that are otherwise not automatically registered and in overcoming document gaps, as well as on user experience. The proposed test of the 'trusted intermediary' consent model would provide data on its uptake and effect on support access for non-digital users.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in and a clear record of which data was used. The proposed test of the 'pre-emptive information' channel is a planned mitigation aimed directly at building trust around these concerns. The 'trusted intermediary' model introduces additional data-sharing considerations, which the proposed small-scale test would aim to evaluate. The integrated document upload function would require robust security, which would be a focus of the small-scale test design. Wrong eligibility decisions would be reduced by keeping a human review step for edge cases.

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems. The proposal includes a planned small-scale test of a 'decline feedback' channel, asking beneficiaries who decline automated offers to optionally share their reasons, to improve targeting and communication. Furthermore, the proposal includes a planned small, targeted test of a 'pre-emptive information' channel. This test would send a brief, plain-language summary of data usage and privacy safeguards alongside the initial offer message, aiming to build trust and increase opt-in rates. Additionally, the proposal includes a planned, small-scale test of a 'reverse notification' feature. This would allow users to proactively and securely flag a life event (e.g., job loss) within the government app to trigger the automated eligibility check, providing a bridge for events not automatically captured by registration systems. This proposed test of the 'reverse notification' feature would also include integrating it with a secure, verifiable document upload function for the single most common missing document (e.g., a termination letter), to bridge the gap for events not fully captured in government records. The proposed test would also include a 'life event confirmation receipt' that users can save or share, providing them with a tangible record of their proactive notification to the government. The proposal also includes a planned small-scale test of a 'trusted intermediary' consent model. In this test, a citizen could authorize a pre-vetted community organization (e.g., a local family center) to receive and help them understand the automated offer on their behalf, specifically for non-digital users.

## Delivery Model

The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A proposed enhancement to this model is a hypothetical partnership with a select number of trusted, non-governmental community organizations to act as 'digital navigators' for the phone line and service centers. These navigators would specifically assist non-digital users in understanding and responding to the automated offers, thereby testing an enhanced inclusion model. The proposed test of the 'trusted intermediary' consent model would be integrated into this navigator partnership, allowing authorized organizations to act as formal intermediaries for consenting users. A small central team would maintain the eligibility rules, and each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

Most government services wait for people to apply. This proposal reverses the direction: the government would come to the citizen at the moment of need, which is rare in social services.
